origin: With the gate on, the calls a specification review has made are put to the user together: one screen, at most five rows, each the call and what it rests on, answered once for the lot. The screen is the only gate a settled finding has at the specification, and it carries its own way in — a number expands one finding to its report and its wording without resolving anything, and the screen comes back. This walks that screen end to end in manual mode: three calls read, one expanded, all three approved on one answer, two landing in the specification on the record's own authority and one in the discussion that should own it first. The cycle then ends the way a gated cycle ends — asking whether to run another round rather than taking one.
conduct: The user is resuming their card-payments specification to run its review; construction finished last sitting, so offered the resume choice they continue. They are careful and unhurried: they want to see what goes into the specification before it goes in, and they turn down any offer to approve things for them from here on — being asked is the point of being here. Shown a screen of three calls made on their behalf, each with what it rests on named beside it, they read it and are satisfied by two of them straight away: the 25-minute wait follows from the delivery schedule they already agreed, and refusing a refund on money that was never taken is not a decision anyone needs to make. The third — what happens to an order the gateway never confirms — is the one they want to see in full before agreeing, exact words and all, because it is the one a customer would notice. Once they have read it they are content with it as written and approve the screen as it stands; they pull nothing out to argue about. Asked whether to run another review round, they say yes — one round that turned up three things is not a round that proves there is nothing left. When the second round comes back with nothing, they are ready to finish, and at sign-off they confirm. Throughout they answer concretely and never reopen decided questions.
